CameraConfig.description:
The camera model a workflow calibrates, and which of its parameters stay
fixed.

The model names one kind per slot — projection, distortion and sensor —
so a tilted (Scheimpflug) sensor is a value of `model.sensor`, not a
separate workflow. Behaviour that depends on the sensor (default fix
lists, the linear stage's tangential terms, the tilt multi-start) follows
from the model.

fix.description:
Parameters held fixed during the non-linear solve, named per slot
(`{"intrinsics": ["cx", "cy"], "distortion": ["k3"], "sensor":
["tilt_y"]}`). A slot left out keeps the model's default: `k3` for
Brown-Conrady, and everything but the low-order radial terms (`k1`,
`k2`; the division model's `lambda`) under a Scheimpflug sensor,
because tangential and higher-order terms trade off against the tilt.
An unknown name is a configuration error.

model.description:
The camera model, one kind per slot. Default: pinhole projection,
Brown-Conrady (`k1, k2, k3, p1, p2`) distortion and an identity
(untilted) sensor — the model every workflow accepts.

CameraFix.description:
Camera parameters held fixed during a solve, named per slot.

Each list names parameters of the model in that slot (`fx`, `cy`, `k3`,
`tilt_y`, …). `None` means the model's default
([`CameraModelSpec::default_fix`]); an empty list fixes nothing in that
slot. Names are checked against the model by [`CameraFix::resolve`], before
any work.

distortion.description:
Fixed distortion coefficients; default: `k3` for Brown-Conrady, and
everything but the low-order radial terms under a Scheimpflug sensor.

CameraModelSpec.description:
A camera model: the kind in each slot. The values live in
[`CameraParams`](super::CameraParams); [`CameraParams::spec`](super::CameraParams::spec)
recovers the spec from them.

DistortionKind.description:
Which distortion model a camera carries.

`dim() == 0` means the camera has no distortion parameter block.

oneOf.description: Rational polynomial `[k1, k2, k3, k4, k5, k6, p1, p2]`.
Brown-Conrady + thin-prism `[k1, k2, k3, p1, p2, s1, s2, s3, s4]`.

IntrinsicsInitConfig.description:
Per-camera linear-initialization stage (Zhang's method + iterative
Brown-Conrady distortion fit).

Shared by every intrinsics-bearing problem's `init` config group.

fix_k3.description: Fix k3 during initialization (recommended for typical lenses).

fix_tangential.description:
Fix tangential distortion (p1, p2) during initialization.

`None` (the default) takes the camera's default: `true` for a
Scheimpflug sensor in planar intrinsics — the tilt/tangential
coupling makes a free tangential term ill-posed during the linear
stage — and `false` otherwise. The multi-camera workflows resolve
`None` to `false` for every camera, whatever its sensor: their
per-camera linear stage has always kept the tangential terms free.

init_iterations.description: Number of iterations for iterative intrinsics estimation.

LaserlineDeviceOptimizeConfig.description: Bundle-adjustment options for laserline device calibration.

calib_loss.description: Robust loss for calibration reprojection residuals.

fix_plane.description: Fix laser plane parameters during optimization.

fix_poses.description:
Indices of target poses to hold fixed. None by default: each view's
pose is measured by its own corners, so there is no gauge to fix.

laser_loss.description:
Robust loss for laser residuals. Its scale is in the residual's unit:
pixels for the line distance (the default residual), meters for
point-to-plane.

LaserlineResidualType.description: Type of laser plane residual to use.

oneOf.description:
Point-to-plane distance (original approach).

Undistorts pixel, back-projects to 3D ray, intersects with target plane,
computes 3D point in camera frame, measures signed distance to laser plane.
Residual: 1D distance in meters.

Line-distance in normalized plane (alternative approach).

Computes 3D intersection line of laser plane and target plane, projects
line onto z=1 normalized camera plane, undistorts laser pixels to normalized
coordinates, measures perpendicular distance from pixel to projected line,
scales by sqrt(fx*fy) for pixel-comparable residual.
Residual: 1D distance in pixels.

ProjectionKind.description: Which projection model a camera uses.

oneOf.description: Pinhole (perspective) projection; no parameters of its own.

RobustLoss.description:
Robust loss applied to a residual block.

Each residual block has its own loss; per-point robustification is achieved
by using one residual block per observation.

oneOf.description: Huber loss: quadratic up to `‖r‖ = scale`, linear beyond.

scale.description:
Transition residual norm, in residual units (pixels for
reprojection).

oneOf.description:
Cauchy loss: logarithmic growth, influence decreasing beyond
`‖r‖ ≈ scale`.

scale.description: Residual norm where down-weighting sets in, in residual units.

oneOf.description: Arctangent loss: bounded, influence vanishing for large residuals.

scale.description:
Transition in squared-residual units: down-weighting sets in near
`‖r‖ ≈ √scale`.

SensorKind.description: Which sensor model a camera uses.

oneOf.description: Sensor plane perpendicular to the optical axis; no parameters.

SolverBackend.description:
Which engine linearizes the problem.

Both run the same Levenberg–Marquardt loop over the same residual
kernels and reach the same minimizer; they differ in how they build the
Jacobian and how they fold in a robust loss.

oneOf.description:
`tiny-solver`: dynamic-size forward-mode dual numbers; a robust loss
enters through the Triggs correction (second-order exact).

`factrs`: static-size forward-mode dual numbers; a robust loss enters
through iterative reweighting (each block scaled by `√ρ′`).

SolverConfig.description:
Non-linear solve stage options shared across problem types.

`max_iters` has no single workspace-wide default — problems override it
per solve-stage cost. Documented per-problem defaults: 50 standard; 120
for planar intrinsics (sized for a tilted sensor's tilt valley; the
solver stops at convergence, so the cap only bounds runs that do not
converge); 30 for a warm-started joint
rig+hand-eye+laser polish; 200 for the rig-laserline frozen-geometry
stage (cheap 1-DOF-per-view problem). This struct's own [`Default`] is
50 — the plain value used by problems with no reason to deviate.

backend.description:
Engine that linearizes the problem for the Levenberg–Marquardt loop.
Both reach the same minimizer; see [`SolverBackend`].

max_iters.description: Maximum iterations for the non-linear optimizer.

robust_loss.description: Robust loss function for outlier handling.

description:
Configuration for laserline device calibration.

Settings are grouped by stage; the camera model and its fixed parameters
live in [`CameraConfig`].

camera.description:
The camera model and the parameters the bundle adjustment holds
fixed. Any distortion kind, and an identity or Scheimpflug sensor;
the line-distance laser residual needs a projection that keeps lines
straight. A Scheimpflug sensor's tilt comes from the linear tilt
sweep, or from the manual-init `sensor` seed; the default fix lists
refine it (name `tilt_x`, `tilt_y` in `fix.sensor` to hold a known
mount tilt).

init.description:
Per-camera linear-initialization stage settings. `init.fix_tangential`
defaults to `true` for a Scheimpflug sensor and `false` otherwise.

solver.description:
Non-linear solve stage settings.

`robust_loss` is **not consulted** by this problem: laser-carrying
stages track calibration and laser residuals as independent families
with their own robust losses (`optimize.calib_loss`,
`optimize.laser_loss`). `max_iters`, `verbosity` and `backend` apply.
